page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5i-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, configured with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs. The hardware profile includes 32 GB of system memory, providing a 4.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. Graphics and parallel computing acceleration are delivered via a single integrated NVIDIA Tesla P4 GPU based on the Pascal architecture, equipped with 8 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage and relies on external network storage, operating with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the CPU and memory subsystems exhibit moderate to low performance relative to modern cloud hardware. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is positioned in the bottom 10%, while multi-core performance falls in the bottom 25%. Large-block memory read and write bandwidth benchmarks also rank in the bottom 25%, though cached small-block reads achieve average tier results. Cryptography, compression, and database operations consistently register in the lower performance quartiles. These results highlight a clear tradeoff: the instance provides dedicated GPU resources but relies on older-generation CPU architecture and slower memory throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.gn5i-c8g1.2xlarge offers an entry-level GPU-accelerated tier. It is designed for workloads that require hardware acceleration but do not demand high-performance host CPU processing or high-speed local storage. Suitable workloads include legacy CUDA-based applications, low-density video transcoding, basic deep learning inference, and lightweight graphics rendering.
